messages.author: 7a4a5fe753932e1a
messages.subject: crash without pardiso
parts:
Hi,

I am running a spatio-temporal model for interpolating monthly temperature data. Everything runs fine when I run my model with a dataset subset. With a larger dataset, the only way to avoid a crash (segmentation fault) is using the PARDISO library. Why R-INLA without PARDISO crashes and without not?

Thanks
Guido

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] crash without pardiso
parts:
with taucs or pardiso with openmp.strategy='pardiso.serial', then the
parallisation is done by running serial factorisations on many
matrices in parallel, like

## do this loop in parallel
for(i in 1:n) Q.chol[[i]] = chol(Q[[i]])

this run efficient if the matrices are small enough, AND, there is
enough memory to handle all these

the other strategy, openmp.strategy='pardiso.parallel', is different,
it uses all cores to factorisize ONE, and only ONE, matrix at the
time, like

## do in parallel
Q.chol = chol(Q)

this require much less memory, but is (in most cases) slower then the
serial strategy, IF, the serial strategy can work without any memory
issue.


since TAUCS is serial code only, and PARDISO is serial and parallel
code, then
the serial strategy works for TAUCS and PARDISO, while the parallel
one, only works for PARDISO.

for large models, as you have, yes, then chose
openmp.strategy='pardiso.parallel'

hope this helps,
H
